labeler: Claude (Fable 5.1) working from the context cards in samples/spreadsheetbench.md, 2026-09-14; Claude (Opus 5.5) for the seven FORMULA_DRIFT cards first drawn in samples/spreadsheetbench-summary.md, 2026-09-25, for the cards first drawn in samples/spreadsheetbench-040.md, 2026-09-30, and for the DUPLICATE_KEY cards first drawn in samples/spreadsheetbench-dk.md, 2026-10-04. Every label carries a reason so a maintainer can overrule it.
protocol: TP: the finding points at something a careful reviewer would want to look at, for the reason the rule gives. FP: the rule misread the workbook. unsure: the card was not enough to decide; excluded from precision.

rule_notes.BLANK_PRECEDENT: Was 15,300 findings at 4% precision on 0.2.0 (guarded formulas, template rows, mirror links, blank-ignoring aggregates); positional and guarded uses, blank-tolerant functions, rows with no inputs and sparse columns were then excluded and 29 findings remained, none of them a defect: a ledger with paired amount columns (debit or credit, buying or selling) where the blank is a zero by design, plus empty rows inside a block. Since 0.4.0 the rule is off by default and does not run on this corpus; turn it on for data that must never have gaps.
rule_notes.BROKEN_REFERENCE: Right every time: #REF! formulas, and external links now reported as one Info note per source workbook per sheet (was one High finding per cell).
rule_notes.CIRCULAR_REFERENCE: Positional idioms (ROWS(A$6:A8), COLUMNS($D7:AA7), ROW(A19)) and the CELL("filename",Q2) sheet-name idiom were 23 of 25 findings on 0.2.0 and are gone. What remains is the deliberate IFERROR(1/(1/F8)) date-freeze self-reference (which needs iterative calculation) and a MAX(B$7:B377)+1 counter that includes its own cell; both are worth a reviewer's attention.
rule_notes.DUPLICATE_KEY: Only a range a first-match lookup searches counts (VLOOKUP first column, HLOOKUP first row, MATCH/XLOOKUP lookup array), and since the duplicate-key rework each searched range is read on its own along its search direction: a label repeated down a column across separate HLOOKUP blocks is no longer a duplicate. Repeats a first-match lookup cannot get wrong are skipped: a range that looks for the next occurrence, three or more identical keys together (detail rows under one ID), occurrences returning the same values (countries sharing USD at 1), categories where every key repeats three times or more, and repeats told apart by a date beside them (validity periods, a dated log); error values are not keys. That took the rule from 69 findings to 39. True positives: postcodes shared by two schools in a MATCH column, menu items and products listed twice, letters listed twice in a rate table, a product heading two bins in one HLOOKUP row so a SUM of HLOOKUPs misses one, a weekday row repeated per week where MATCH finds only week one, and a growing lookup that returns the oldest sale. False positives left: header labels repeated in a searched row but never looked up (checking the actual lookup values would remove them), a label written over a column pair, and composite keys whose formula ignores the second key (group plus material, region plus expense).
rule_notes.FORMULA_DRIFT: 0 of 25 on 0.2.0. Rows of unrelated columns, chain seeds, label-link columns that step through another sheet, and short or header-labelled totals rows mixing SUM and AVERAGE are exempt; a SUM that became an AVERAGE inside a longer run of totals is still reported, because that is the 'function replaced' fault the EUSES corpus injects. What remains is mostly real: a first row whose SUMPRODUCT differs from the rows below and evaluates to #VALUE!, a DB() call missing an argument, a typed threshold of 90120 where the rows around use 90, a total that starts one row late, a typed input inside a fill (=525*1.5 beside =BF24*1.5), and a manual override link. Summary cells that are not part of the run beside them are exempt too: a link heading a column of labels (L2 = M14 over a column of names, where the run's SUM would add up text) and one of a row of counts over one block (COUNTIF(F5:F11,1), 2 and 3). Of the six findings this removed, the four already labeled were FP or unsure, and EUSES recall did not move. Remaining false positives are summary or totals rows whose different formula is the design (a ratio of totals, a 'planned' row that averages under rows that sum, a wins row that counts under an 'average' header) and example sheets where every cell is a different formula. In the 0.4.0 sample two false positives compute exactly what their neighbours do in another spelling ($-anchored references to the same cells, SUM(x) around a product); comparing the cells a formula resolves to would remove them.
rule_notes.HARDCODE_IN_FORMULA_BLOCK: 8% on 0.2.0: input columns between two formula columns sharing a pattern (running sums, unit x quantity). Those are now recognised from the other axis, and the true positives dominate: a constant typed over an IF, a difference, a rolling sum or a scaled copy in a column of identical formulas. Remaining false positives are input columns on sparse sheets or one-row tables, where the cells above and below the constant are empty and the check has nothing to compare, and input columns whose neighbouring formula lines hold plugs of their own. In the 0.4.0 sample the four false positives are the Actual input columns of one budget workbook family.
rule_notes.HIDDEN_STRUCTURE_IN_TOTAL: Hidden helper columns feeding scores, hidden rows still counted by SUMIFS, hidden lookup tables and hidden source sheets: every sampled finding was a disclosure a reviewer wants. AGGREGATE and SUBTOTAL variants that skip hidden rows no longer count, and hidden rows feeding the same formulas are reported together.
rule_notes.IFERROR_MASK: Since 0.4.0 a wrapper is reported only when its expression can really fail (a division, a lookup, an average, a text or date conversion, arithmetic on a cell) and the fallback reads as a real value; IFNA counts only what returns #N/A, and errors an ISNUMBER or inner IFERROR absorbs, conversions that fall back to the text they read, second lookups, messages and NA() are skipped. That took the rule from 1,763 findings at 28% to 644 at 60%. True positives: Google Sheets placeholder formulas, lookups that turn a missing age, stay or date into 0, averages and ratios that show 0 when there is nothing to average, and a payment schedule. False positives: one order-sheet layout where a site missing from a lookup really is 0 units (several copies in the sample), ranked lists whose end is a blank, and a 0 returned into a text column such as Gender, which the rule cannot tell from a number column.
rule_notes.LITERAL_CONSTANT: Function-slot literals (column indexes, type codes, string positions, date parts, criteria) and the unit constants 60/3600 are skipped, and one finding per formula pattern replaces one per cell. Since 0.4.0 the value a rounding or formatting function works on is checked too (ROUND(A1*1.0725,2) reports 1.0725, not the 2), and a 3 or 6 dividing MONTH() is a calendar fact. True positives are thresholds and assumptions: 37.5 hours, a 90-day cutoff, bonus caps and rates, minimum sample sizes, lead times, pay multipliers, payment terms. One >=10 minimum-sample threshold repeated across many cells with different criteria counts as many patterns. Remaining false positives are calendar grid offsets, ROW() comparisons, literals that mirror a column header, RANDBETWEEN bounds, a MATCH()+3 row offset, and codes returned by IF. The count rose from 1,015 in 0.3.0 because the old report cap had hidden these findings in workbooks flooded by live errors.
rule_notes.LIVE_ERROR: Every sampled finding was a real error value: #REF! formulas, lookups missing their keys, #VALUE! from external links or text arithmetic, #DIV/0! averages with nothing to average, array formulas entered without array evaluation, and error constants pasted into data. Since 0.4.0 an error filled down a column is one finding listing its cells, and the cells an error cycle feeds are listed with it; a #REF! can also be reported by BROKEN_REFERENCE on the same cell.
rule_notes.MERGED_CELL_IN_DATA_RANGE: 0 of 25 on 0.2.0 (titles, headers, labels, merged dates whose formulas already fetch the last non-blank value) and 0 of 24 after the first pass (merged title formulas, merged net lines in totals rows, merged weekly limits). Only a merged number read through a range reference now counts; the rule no longer fires on this corpus and keeps its seeded case.
rule_notes.NUMBERS_STORED_AS_TEXT: The 'referenced by a formula' variant needs a numeric consumer and skips leading-zero identifiers and codes that are only compared; since 0.4.0 it is one finding per column, and text numbers that every formula converts first (--A1, VALUE, *1) are a Low note. True positives are ID and count columns that mix text and numeric forms, a pasted amount with a non-breaking space, and batch numbers in both forms. The false positives were free-text notes columns holding a few bare numbers.
rule_notes.RANGE_EXCLUSION: Four true positives (a total whose siblings span all rows while it stops early); the running COUNT($A$9:A9) false positives are exempt.
rule_notes.RANGE_INCLUDES_SUBTOTAL: The three 0.2.0 findings were a carried-forward total; the constants variant was dropped and the rule no longer fires on this corpus. Its seeded double-count case still passes.
rule_notes.RANGE_LENGTH_MISMATCH: Every remaining finding is COUNT(D87:F89) in a column of COUNT(D87:F87) formulas, a real fill error in one family of bowling sheets; one-cell links and disjoint debit/credit groups no longer fire.
rule_notes.VOLATILE_FUNCTION: TODAY/NOW are one Info note per sheet, which is the right weight; RAND/RANDBETWEEN feeding analyses, INDIRECT-built addresses and OFFSET over #REF! are reported per pattern. All worth a look at their level.
rule_notes.WHITESPACE_KEY: 8% on 0.2.0 (fixed-width export padding, indentation, headers, spacer cells). Export-padded columns get one Info note, headers and indentation are skipped, and since 0.4.0 the stray padded keys of a column are one finding that names them all. True positives: a padded name among clean ones, a status with a trailing space beside the formula that compares it, leading spaces on postcodes that break a URN match, a trailing newline that turns a duration into #VALUE!. Remaining false positives: header cells below the first rows ("Grade ", "Week "), report dumps with fixed-width text, captions and prose, and uniformly padded account names in a short list.
rule_notes.WHOLE_COLUMN_REFERENCE: COUNTIF/SUMIF/VLOOKUP/MATCH/INDEX over whole columns are bounded by Excel and no longer fire, even inside array formulas. Every remaining finding is an array evaluation over a million rows: IF(A2=ZORD!A:A,...), MAX(IF(F:F=...)), LOOKUP(2,1/(J:J<>"")), SUMPRODUCT over whole columns.
